memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "He spent the night there, and from what he had with him he selected a gift for his brother Esau: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams, thirty female camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, and twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys. He put them in the care of his servants, each herd by itself, and said to his servants, 'Go ahead of me, and keep some space between the herds'" - Gen 32:13-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After praying, Jacob prepares a gift for Esau — and what a lavish gift it is. Hundreds of goats, sheep, camels, cattle, and donkeys, sent ahead in wave after wave. This was no token present; it was a costly, generous offering, given from a heart that longed to make peace with the brother he had wronged.

There is something instructive in Jacob's willingness to give so much. He was not trying to hold on to every last animal; he was ready to part with a great deal for the sake of reconciliation. Peace mattered more to him than possessions. Having once cheated his brother, he now poured out his wealth to seek his brother's favour.

This reminds us that reconciliation often costs something. Making peace can mean swallowing our pride, giving up our "rights," offering more than seems fair, or generously making amends for a past wrong. Cheap words alone rarely heal deep rifts; genuine reconciliation usually asks something of us.

Jesus taught that being reconciled to a brother matters so much that we should even leave our gift at the altar to go and make things right (Matt 5:23-24). If you have wronged someone, consider what generous step you might take toward peace. Reconciliation is worth the cost.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Are you willing to give generously for the sake of peace?
Where might reconciliation cost you pride, rights, or resources?
Is there a wrong you need to make amends for generously?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to value peace more than possessions or pride. Show me the generous steps I can take toward reconciliation, and give me a heart willing to make amends. Amen.
